ai.description: This slender colubrid reaches 1.2 meters. It is yellowish-brown with black-edged, white-spotted crossbars and two prominent dark stripes on the neck. A distinct black streak extends behind each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Coelognathus helena* is the pair of distinct, dark, longitudinal stripes on the nape of the neck, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Trinket Snake inhabits diverse environments, ranging from dry deciduous forests and scrublands to agricultural fields, typically at elevations from sea level up to 2,000m.
ai.behavior: The Trinket Snake is primarily diurnal and actively hunts for rodents and lizards, often displaying a defensive posture by flattening its neck when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Coelognathus helena* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 5–12 eggs. Breeding generally occurs from March to May, with hatching often observed in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Coelognathus helena* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to southern India, typically below 2,000 meters elevation.
